result.title: Equal-information evaluation of credit assignment in modular financial reinforcement learning
result.summary: Credit assignment in modular financial reinforcement learning is difficult to evaluate because an attributed signal may improve a component loss without adding decision-relevant information or improving economic outcomes. We propose an evaluation framework combining equal-information reconstruction controls, fixed-utility comparisons and prespecified downstream guardrails. The framework is instantiated in an attribution-guided modular trading architecture and tested in three controlled studies covering update allocation, supervision-target representation and portfolio risk control. We find that residual-based allocation is exactly reproduced by an ordinary loss-budget control under the disclosed interface; direct shortfall supervision improves component prediction but fails decoded-outcome preservation; and component-wise critic supervision worsens risk-condition certainty equivalent and drawdown relative to scalar supervision under fixed utility. These results identify three distinct evaluation failures: redundant attribution signals, representation-induced prediction trade-offs, and misalignment between component supervision and downstream risk outcomes. A preserved historical engineering case further shows why module-level learning claims require run-level provenance. The contribution is a reusable methodology for evaluating credit assignment in expert systems operating under partial observability, delayed feedback and economic risk constraints.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对模块化金融强化学习中信用分配难以评估的问题，提出结合等信息重构对照、固定效用比较与预设下游守护条件的评估框架，并在更新分配、监督目标表示与组合风险控制三项受控研究中诊断出冗余归因信号等三类评估失败。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「等信息重构对照＋固定效用比较」的评估方法可能可供核查：用于判断被归因的信号（如 latent 状态）是否真正带来决策相关信息，对应 LVR 中贡献分配与「答案是否使用 latent 内容」的评估问题，但金融域差异较大、迁移仅为推测。
